subject.title: Add a retraction window for forwarded exec approvals (agent-cancellable hold before prompt delivery)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in agent-originated hold/retract contract for forwarded exec approvals, and what Gateway config, RPC, audit, and Codex/native failure semantics are acceptable?
rationale: The request is technically plausible but changes human approval timing and command-execution safety semantics across public config, Gateway protocol, channel delivery, and Codex approval contracts; automation cannot choose that product boundary safely.

options.title: Design opt-in core hold/retract
options.body: Accept a default-off `holdMs` feature only after maintainers define audited retraction, fail-open prompt delivery, fail-closed execution, protocol/schema, and Codex/native behavior.

options.title: Defer core retraction
options.body: Keep current immediate delivery semantics and address prompt noise through existing approval policy, safer command formation, or narrower dedupe/timeout fixes.

options.title: Narrow to adjacent approval issues first
options.body: Prioritize existing duplicate-prompt, timeout, or channel-routing approval issues before adding a new agent-originated cancellation contract.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core hold/retract
recommendation.body: Accept a default-off `holdMs` feature only after maintainers define audited retraction, fail-open prompt delivery, fail-closed execution, protocol/schema, and Codex/native behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The approval framework and manager/forwarder history make this the strongest routing signal for a design decision across the central approval contract.
